title: VI Translator: play GTA VI in your language
description: VI Translator reads GTA VI's subtitles from your screen and shows them translated, live, over the game: on your PC, in OBS, or on your TV. Free.
hero_sub: VI Translator reads the game's subtitles from your screen and shows them translated, live, over the game: on your PC, in OBS, or on your TV.
demo_en_2: Press [A] to get in the car.
demo_en_3: We hit the bank at midnight.
demo_label: An example: the English line, and the translation drawn over the game
features_title: Everything the game says, in your language
features_sub: It reads the picture like a viewer would, translates, and draws the translation where you need it.
f1_text: Dialogue and on-screen instructions are translated as they appear, and placed over the game.
f2_text: Menus, mission results and captions are translated as well, with support for each screen arriving through automatic updates.
f3_text: Highlighted words keep their colors, and controller buttons stay in place, so instructions read like the game's own.
f4_text: It only reads the picture: from the game window, a capture card or OBS. No mods, no game files, no memory.
f5_text: The app itself speaks 33 languages, including right-to-left layouts.
f6_text: When a new version is out it asks first, checks its signature, and restarts.
where_sub: One app on your PC. The translation goes where you look.
w1_title: Over the game on your PC
w1_text: A clean overlay on top of the game window, with the text style you choose.
w2_text: A browser source for streamers: the translation lands on the game picture in your scene.
w3_text: The VI Translator TV app draws it over the console's HDMI picture, on Google TV, Android TV, LG and Samsung TVs.
w4_text: Read the live translations on any device on your home network.
how_sub: Four steps, a couple of minutes.
s1_text: It's portable: nothing to install. Windows, Linux and macOS.
s2_text: The game window, your capture card, or an OBS source.
s3_text: Your language and a translation service: a free offline model, DeepL, Azure, Google, LibreTranslate or Claude.
s4_text: Choose the Grand Theft Auto VI profile and play. The translations appear as the game speaks.
langs_list: Arabic · Hindi · Bengali · Urdu · Indonesian · Turkish · Vietnamese · Persian · Thai · Tamil · Telugu · Marathi · Ukrainian · Dutch · Filipino · Malay · Swahili · Romanian · Greek · Czech
dl_sub: Free, portable executables. Get the one for your system from the latest release.
dl_linux_note: x64 and ARM. Needs WebKitGTK 4.1 and Tesseract (English).
dl_macos_note: Apple silicon. Not tested on a Mac yet.
privacy_text: "Help improve translations" is on by default: every few minutes it sends the English lines you saw (subtitles, instructions, captions) to the project's server, so they can be translated better for everyone. It's anonymous: a random install ID, no account, no screenshots, and never menus, where player names appear. Turn it off in the Advanced tab and nothing more is sent.
a1: Yes. The app is free, with a free offline translator for some languages. Online services like DeepL or Google use your own key and their own pricing.
q2: Does it change or touch the game?
a2: No. It only reads the picture, the same way a capture or streaming app does. It doesn't touch the game's files or memory.
q3: I play on PS5 or Xbox. What do I need?
a3: A PC, and either a capture card or your console's remote play app. With a card that has passthrough, the console goes into the card and the card into your TV, so you play with no delay while the PC reads the picture. No capture card? Stream your console to the PC with PS Remote Play or the Xbox app, and read its window. The picture quality and delay depend on your network.
q4: What do I need for the TV app?
a4: A Google TV or Android TV, an LG TV with webOS 5 or newer, or a Samsung Smart TV from 2018 or later, with the console plugged into it through the capture card's passthrough, and VI Translator running on a PC on the same home network.
a5: It translates into 20 languages, and the app's own interface comes in 33.
a6: The free offline translator works on your PC for some languages. Other languages use an online translation service.
q7: What is sent from my PC?
a7: Only if "Help improve translations" is on (it is by default): the English lines you saw, anonymously, never menus or screenshots. See Privacy above.

setups_title: Set it up in two steps
setups_sub: First choose how VI Translator sees the game, then where you see the translation.
st1_text: How VI Translator sees the game: a capture card copies the console's picture to the PC, and a remote play app streams it over your home network.
st2_title: Choose where you see the translation
st2_text: On your TV, on the PC, on a phone or in your stream: each works with the source you picked, and you can use several at once.
shot_illustration: Illustration: the TV app's drawing over a stand-in picture
sa_text: The best way to read a PS5 or Xbox: the picture is sharp, and with a passthrough card you play on your TV with no delay while the PC reads a copy.
sa_need: A PC · A capture card with HDMI passthrough · Your console
sa_1: Console HDMI into the card's input, the card's passthrough output into your TV, and the card's USB into the PC.
sa_2: In VI Translator, Source tab: pick your capture card.
sa_3: Translator tab: pick your language and a translation service.
sa_4: Then choose where you see the translation, in step 2.
sa_shot_1: Source tab: the capture card, with the translation drawn over the picture
sa_shot_2: Translator tab: the language and the translation service
sa_tip_1: Pick a card with HDMI passthrough, 4K if your TV is 4K: you keep playing on the TV at full quality with no delay, while the PC gets a copy.
sa_tip_2: On PS5, turn off HDCP (Settings › System › HDMI › Enable HDCP), or the card gets no picture.
sa_tip_3: The PC only reads its copy of the picture: 1080p is plenty to read the subtitles.
sb_title: Over the game, on your TV
sb_text: The TV app draws the translation over the console's HDMI picture, in the same places as on the PC. With a 4K passthrough card, the TV keeps the console's full 4K picture.
sb_need: The capture card setup · A Google TV or Android TV, an LG TV (webOS 5 or newer) or a Samsung TV (2018 or later)
sb_1: On the TV, install Downloader from Google Play, open it and enter the code [[3156727]], then install VI Translator.
sb_2: Open it: it shows a 6-digit code, and keeps waiting 10 minutes if you switch the TV to your PC.
sb_3: On the PC: Source tab, Show on a TV, Connect a TV. Type the code and press Connect.
sb_4: Switch to your console's input and play. Choose "Show on" to keep the translation on that input only.
sb_shot_2: Connect a TV, on the PC
sl_text: LG's store doesn't allow apps that draw over another input, so the LG app is installed with LG's free Developer Mode. As on Android TV, the translation shows over the console's input. For LG TVs with webOS 5 or newer (2020 and later).
sl_1: Make a free account at webostv.developer.lge.com. On the TV, install Developer Mode from the LG Content Store, sign in, turn on Dev Mode Status (the TV restarts), then turn on Key Server.
sl_2: On your PC, install the free webOS Dev Manager, add your TV with its IP address and the passphrase shown in Developer Mode, then install the VI Translator .ipk file from its latest release (links below).
sl_3: Open VI Translator on the TV and connect it from the PC with its 6-digit code, as above. Press Back to hide its screen and switch to the console's input: the translation shows over it.
sl_4: Open the app again after turning the TV on or pressing Home. Developer Mode runs out after a while: extend it in the Developer Mode app, or the TV removes the app.
ss_text: Samsung TVs let no app draw over another input, so the Samsung app shows the console's HDMI input itself, with the translation on top: open the app instead of switching the TV to the console. For Samsung Smart TVs from 2018 and later.
ss_1: On the TV, open Apps, press 1 2 3 4 5 on the remote, turn on Developer mode and enter the IP address of the PC or Android phone you'll install from as the Host PC IP. Then restart the TV.
ss_2: On that PC or phone, install the free Apps2Samsung, and add [[github.com/vi-translator/vi-translator-tizen-tv]] as one of your own sources.
ss_3: Choose your TV, then VI Translator, and press Install. The first time, Apps2Samsung asks you to sign in to your Samsung account to make its signing certificate.
ss_4: Open VI Translator on the TV and connect it from the PC with its 6-digit code, as above. Press OK for the menu, where you choose the console's HDMI input.
sc_title: Console through a remote play app
sc_text: No capture card? Stream your console to the PC with PS Remote Play or the Xbox app, and read its window. The picture quality and delay depend on your network.
sc_need: A PC · PS Remote Play or the Xbox app
sc_1: Start PS Remote Play or the Xbox app on the PC and connect to your console.
sc_2: In VI Translator, Source tab: pick the remote play window.
sc_3: Pick your language in the Translator tab, then play in the remote play window: the translation shows over it.
sc_shot_1: Source tab: the remote play window
sc_tip_1: Connect the console, and the PC if you can, with a network cable: the picture is sharper and steadier.
sc_tip_2: Set the remote play app to its highest resolution, and don't minimize its window.
sc_tip_3: You play in that window on the PC, with a controller connected to the PC, so remote play's own delay applies.
sp_title: In VI Translator, on your PC
sp_text: VI Translator's Play mode shows the game picture with the translation drawn on it, where the game's own text is. Double-click it for full screen and play right there.
sp_1: Set up your source and language in Setup mode.
sp_2: Switch to Play mode, at the top of the app.
sp_3: Double-click the picture for full screen. With a passthrough card, you can also keep playing on the TV and read the translation on the PC screen.
sp_shot_1: Play mode: the live translations, and the picture with the overlay
se_title: For streamers: translations for your viewers
se_text: Add the translation to your stream as an OBS browser source: it lands on the game picture in your scene, so your viewers read it too.
se_need: OBS Studio · Any of the setups above
se_1: In VI Translator, read your capture card, or a source in OBS (turn on OBS's WebSocket server and connect).
se_2: In OBS, add a Browser Source above your game with the address the app shows (http://127.0.0.1:8790/obs), sized like your canvas.
se_3: Go live: the translation follows the game, with the text style you set.
se_shot_1: Source tab: OBS, and the browser source address
sf_text: Read the translations on a second screen: any phone, tablet or computer on your home network, in a browser. Handy when your TV can't run the TV app.
sf_need: Any of the setups above · A phone or tablet on the same Wi-Fi
sf_1: In VI Translator, Source tab: turn on Share on my home network.
sf_2: Scan the QR code, or open the address the app shows, on your phone.
sf_3: The live translations appear as the game speaks. Make the text bigger or smaller with A+ and A−.
sf_shot_1: Share on my home network: the address and its QR code
sf_shot_2: The live translations on a phone
